assessments.reasoning: The 2010 discussion specifies a leading row marker comprising multiple inputs or outputs and explains matching row-variable names across nested and outer effects. The each example ties the same row through enclosing and nested effects and permits different stack group sizes.

challenge.method: Compared the polymorphic example across its single-value and two-value extra-stack cases, and checked ordinary fixed-effect words and the paper's separate static stack-height checking.
challenge.results: The row variable describes a group of stack entries and unifies corresponding rows. No run-time value types or all-words polymorphism follow.

limitations: This is the 2010 notation description, with no claim that row variables specify runtime value types or that every ordinary word is row-polymorphic.
